cards.explanation: The answer is the Passover. Jesus tells His disciples, "You know that the Passover is two days away…" He says it right alongside the news that the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified. The clock is ticking, friends, and Jesus is the one who names the days. (Matthew 26:2)

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified." In Mark 2:10, Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself, so He is talking about His own road. I think this one is hard to hear. (Matthew 26:2)

The answer is that they plot to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him. The text says they "…conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him." Covertly means quietly, out of sight, friends. And they plot it in the courtyard of the high priest, Caiaphas. (Matthew 26:3-4)

The answer is that there may be a riot among the people. The plotters say, "But not during the feast… or there may be a riot among the people." The text gives the riot as their reason, bakers. That's the worry behind the condition. (Matthew 26:5)

The answer is head. The woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, "…which she poured on His head as He reclined at the table." The text puts it right on His head, friends. Hold onto that detail, because Jesus will say what it means. (Matthew 26:7)

The answer is that they're indignant. The disciples "were indignant" and then they ask, "Why this waste?" Indignant means they were upset at what they saw, friends. The text then says Jesus was "Aware of this…" (Matthew 26:8-10)

The answer is False. The disciples say, "This perfume could have been sold at a high price, and the money given to the poor." In their words, the money goes to the poor, not the temple, bakers. That comes right after they ask, "Why this waste?" (Matthew 26:8-9)

The answer is beautiful. Jesus says, "Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me." The disciples are looking at the cost, friends. Jesus looks at the deed and calls it beautiful. (Matthew 26:10)

The answer is False. Jesus says, "The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me." The poor are the ones who will always be with them, bakers. Jesus is the one they will not always have. (Matthew 26:11)

The answer is that she prepared His body for burial. Jesus says, "By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial." Jesus Himself tells them what her deed was for, friends. I think that gives it a weight the disciples hadn't mentioned. (Matthew 26:12)

The answer is that her deed will be told wherever the gospel is preached. Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her." She poured out one jar at one table, and Jesus says it will be told in all the world. And here we are telling it, bakers. (Matthew 26:13)

The answer is True. Judas, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests and asked, "What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?" He is the one who brings it up, friends. The chief priests answer by setting out silver. (Matthew 26:14-15)

The answer is thirty. The text says, "And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver." Judas asked what they were willing to give, and that was what they set out for him, bakers. The chief priests are the ones who set it out. (Matthew 26:15)
